For this project, our team utilized data from Zillow about the California housing market. We primarily looked at average days on the market, median sale prices over time, average listing prices, median mortgage rate, and median house prices across California.
 
**How did median home sale prices change in California before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic?**
 
Why this question is interesting:
We all know that Covid had an impact on the housing market, but for those of us who were not in a place to worry about buying or selling a house for whatever reason during this time, it may be difficult to fully understand the impact that Covid had. Answering this question gives us a concrete visual of how California housing prices were affected by Covid.
 
Excel Analysis:
To make the chart we started by taking the Median Price data and filtering out all other states except CA.  The median was calculated to see the average change. The x-axis was built using the median prices for 26 California cities. Taking the square root we arrived at 6 bins for the x-axis. The data runs from $350K to $1.59M, a range of $1.24M. A bin width of $250,000 gives 6 bins. 
 
Visual Development:
Our team created an assertion-evidence slide that features the histogram chart that was created to answer this question, and the assertion statement in the heading.
 
Assertion-Evidence Slide:
![Scatter Plot](Histogram.png)

**Which California cities have the highest average housing prices?**
 
Why this question is interesting:
A state as large as California has hundreds cities with varying populations and geographical characteristics. This question helps us look into how different factors affect housing prices, and allows us to compare these affects to other parts of the United States.
 
Excel Analysis:
To make this bar-chart, we started by creating a pivot table of the average listing prices across America. Then, state name and region name were set as the rows, and average listing price from 8/31/2026 as the value. The rows were then filtered to only show data from California. After creating the bar-chart from this filtered data, it was then refined with some axis resizing.
 
Visual Development:
Our team created an assertion-evidence slide that features the bar-chart that was created to answer this question, and the assertion statement in the heading.
 
Assertion-Evidence Slide:
![Scatter Plot](BarChart.png)                                                                                      

 **How are housing days on market distributed across individual property listings?**
 
Why this question is interesting:
Analyzing the number of days a property is on the market can provide some valuable information about the area it is in, and the people who live there.
 
Excel Analysis:
The data was formatted such that each column is a year and each row is a month. This allows us to turn the 9 years of data into 9 lines making it easy to see trends by month and trends over years.
 
Visual Development:
Our team created an assertion-evidence slide that features the times series graph that was created to answer this question, and the assertion statement in the heading.
 
Assertion-Evidence Slide:
![Scatter Plot](TimeSeries.png)                                                                                        

 **What relationship exists between mortgage interest rates for single-family homes with a 20% down payment and median single-family home prices across California cities?**
 
Why this question is interesting:
This question showcases how expensive it is/ would be to buy a house in California, and even if you aren't planning to move, it still provides some perspective on the cost of living in other areas, like Fayetteville, and a general idea of how mortgage price and house price might be correlated elsewhere.
 
Excel Analysis: 
To answer this question, we uploaded the relevant data into an excel workbook, and used that data to create a dual-axis scatter plot showing how median mortgage rate and median house price relate to eachother across 26 different cities in California. Each Y-axis was then re-formatted to make the data easily readable.
 
Visual Development:
Our team created an assertion-evidence slide that features the scatter-plot that was created to answer this question, and the assertion statement in the heading.
